items.label: Diplomatic Credentials
items.description: A British cultural attaché's identification, supplemented by a visiting scholar's letter from the University of Edinburgh. The signatures are genuine. The name is not.

items.label: Lockpick Wire
items.description: A short length of steel wire, bent at one end. Adequate for a standard pin-tumbler lock.

inner_door.text: The wire finds the pins. You ease the bolt back and hold the door.

items.label: Service Key
items.description: A brass key on a short chain. Unlocks the kitchen inner door. Someone left it in the rack over the worktop.

inner_door.text: The key turns smoothly. The bolt disengages.

items.label: Stairwell Key
items.description: A heavy warded key. Unlocks the fire door on the ground-floor corridor.

stairwell_door.text: The door unlocks. You ease it open without a sound.

items.label: Stairwell Key
items.description: A heavy warded key from the corridor cabinet. A spare, apparently.

stairwell_door.text: The door unlocks. You ease it open without a sound.

items.label: Stairwell Key
items.description: A heavy warded key taken from Petrov. One of several on the ring.

stairwell_door.text: The door unlocks. You ease it open without a sound.

items.label: Staff Identity Card
items.description: A consulate staff identity card — the name is Morozova, T., Cultural Affairs. The photograph is someone else. Useful if you need to look like you belong.

items.label: Wheelchair
items.description: A standard hospital-issue folding wheelchair. Old but functional. It will take Kuznetsov's weight.

kuznetsov.text: You unfold the wheelchair and position it. Kuznetsov lowers himself into it without comment. He is lighter than he looks.

items.label: Walking Cane
items.description: A plain wooden cane, well-used. Kuznetsov's own — the hospital prescribed it three years ago. He has not used it as much as he should.

kuznetsov.text: You hand him the cane. He takes it, tests his weight, nods. It will do.

items.label: Makarov Pistol
items.description: Standard Soviet sidearm. Eight rounds, reliable, and considerably quieter than a rifle.
